newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold seen in range in absence of impetus.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold seen in range in absence of impetus.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold is expected to consolidate in a $345-$350 price range on Friday after the market shrugged off news that the Bundesank may re-evaluate its gold reserves.
Russian supplies of platinum group metals ultimately hold the key to the near-term direction of the market, analysts said.
GOLD - Chart-wise, little movement was seen on gold's horizon in the immediate term, analysts said.

"The technical indicators continue to drift sideways (partly due to a lack of trading interest) as gold consolidates...A potentially bullish flag pattern is developing as we still slightly favour a re-challenge of overhead resistance," said Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
The market, generally fearful of the prospect of central bank sales, nevertheless registered little lasting reaction to Thursday's news about Germany's central bank.
"There was a little panic at first but now the market has digested the idea. It's clear Germany does not intend to sell gold, just re-evaluate reserves," a trader said.
Gold was also being supported by the dollar's weakness against the yen.
"There was good physical support yesterday out of the Far East. Today the dollar's up a little, but it still makes for cheaper gold than before," the traders said.
At 0800 GMT spot gold was indicated at $347.25/$347.75 per ounce, virtually unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
SILVER - Like gold, silver is drifting in a range.
"The technical indicators appear to be turning in favour of the downside. Also silver appears to be reflecting the slowdown of the platinum rally," Squires said.
At 0800 GMT spot silver was indicated at $4.84/$4.86 per ounce, unchanged from Thursday's New York close.
PLATINUM - The market was still tight and prices would remain firm until Russia started supplying metal, dealers said.
"They have voiced intentions several times, but until they actually start delivering platinum and palladium, prices are going to stay high," a trader said.
At 0800 GMT spot platinum was indicated at $394.00/$395.00 per ounce, up $0.25 from Thursday's New York close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
